NEW YORK, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- vVARDIS () co-founders Dr. Haley Abivardi and Dr. Goly Abivardi aim to reshape the future of dental care with a drill-free treatment for the world's #1 non-communicable disease: cavities.

  • vVARDIS Solves a Problem that Millions Face
    • Tooth decay affects billions of people worldwide, and dental anxiety keeps millions from getting the care they need.
    • vVARDIS is a Swiss dental technology company focused on changing the way early tooth decay is treated.
    • vVARDIS has introduced a new approach that aims to treat decay earlier and more comfortably for patients.
    • Its flagship product, Curodont® Repair Fluoride Plus, uses proprietary peptide technology to help repair early-stage tooth decay by supporting the natural remineralization of enamel --- simply put No drill, No needle, or No filling.
  • Tooth Decay is One of the Most Common Health Issues in the World
    • 2.5 billion people globally live with untreated tooth decay.
    • Nearly 90% of U.S. adults have experienced tooth decay.
    • Nearly 73% of U.S. adults report dental fear.
    • 21% avoid the dentist because of anxiety.
  • The Story that Helped Shape vVARDIS
    • For decades, treating early tooth decay often meant waiting until it worsened or getting a filling. 
    • The founders spent 25 years developing Curodont® Repair Fluoride Plus, a treatment that helps repair early tooth decay before it becomes a cavity.
    • Curodont® gives dentists a way to treat early decay while making the experience easier and less intimidating for patients.
      • The technology has already treated more than 2.5 million teeth
      • Available in more than 20% of U.S. dental practices

data.title: STAR DIAMOND CORPORATION ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS
data.description:
SASKATOON, SK, Nov. 13, 2026 /CNW/ -- Star Diamond Corporation ("Star Diamond" or the "Company") announces its financial and operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are in thousands of Canadian dollars, except common share or per share amounts or as otherwise noted.

The Company's unaudited interim financial statements for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and related management's discussion and analysis are available on the Company's SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca.

OperationsThe Star – Orion South Diamond ProjectAs at the date hereof, the Company's material mineral project is the Star – Orion South Diamond Project (the "Project"). Additional information related to the Project, including the revised mineral resource estimate in respect of the Project, can be found in the technical report relating to the Project, bearing an effective date of July 24, 2024, entitled "Technical Report and Revised Resource Estimate for the Star-Orion South Diamond Project, Fort A La Corne Area, Saskatchewan, Canada", prepared by Daniel C. Leroux, M.Sc. P.Geo., Leon McGarry, B.Sc. P.Geo. and Peter J. Ravenscroft, FAusIMM, a copy of which is available on the Company's SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca.

The Project site is currently under care and maintenance. Star Diamond's technical team will focus on the technical investigation and evaluation of the Project, with the goal of a future development decision. On September 9, 2025, the Company announced the engagement of Misty Clifton and SGS Canada Inc. ("SGS") for a pre-feasibility study on the Project (the "PFS"). The PFS will include a revised statement of mineral reserves for the Project, if warranted, and an economic assessment based thereon. The PFS will enable a feasibility study, on which a production decision can be based. A budget of $3,000 has been prepared for the completion of the PFS.

As of the date hereof, the Company has undertaken work with SGS in respect of PFS engineering services, with expenditures estimated at approximately $137. The work completed to date includes the initial site visit by SGS's qualified persons and initial process design engineering services. The remaining work required to complete the PFS includes mining engineering, cost estimation and civil engineering, along with hydrogeological and geotechnical engineering. The Company currently estimates that the remaining work will require approximately $2,863 and will be completed within approximately 12 months after the necessary financing has been obtained, the required contractors have been scheduled and the work has recommenced.

The Company's inability to obtain sufficient financing has delayed the original plan for the PFS. The timing and scope of the remaining work will depend on the amount and timing of financing available to the Company.

Fort à la Corne Project (Orion North, Orion Centre and Taurus)The Orion North, Orion Centre and Taurus kimberlite clusters form part of the Fort à la Corne Project located in Saskatchewan, Canada. There were no material developments with respect to such clusters during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and the Company is currently reviewing the project to determine future technical, economic, permitting, social and environmental work.

BH ProjectThe Buffalo Hills Diamond Project (the "BH Project") is located in north central, Alberta. There were no material developments with respect to the BH Project during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and the Company is currently reviewing the BH Project to determine future technical, economic, permitting, social and environmental work.

Corporate Developments during 2026On February 4, 2026, the Company granted 41,000,000 stock options to directors, officers, and employees of the Company pursuant to the Company's stock option plan dated April 1, 2024 (the "2024 Stock Option Plan"). The stock options have an exercise price of $0.05 per share, with 1/3 of the options vesting immediately and 1/3 vesting on each of the first and second anniversaries of the date of grant. The stock options expire on the fifth anniversary of the date of grant.

On March 25, 2026, the Company announced the appointment of Brendan F. Moore to the Company's board of directors. Along with the appointment, the Company also granted him 5,000,000 stock options pursuant to the 2024 Stock Option Plan. The stock options have an exercise price of $0.05 per share, with 1/3 of the options vesting immediately and 1/3 vesting on each of the first and second anniversaries of the date of grant. The stock options expire on the fifth anniversary of the date of grant.

On April 28, 2026, the Company entered into a loan agreement (the "Loan Agreement") with Spirit Resources s.a.r.l ("Spirit"). Pursuant to the terms of the Loan Agreement, Spirit advanced an unsecured loan in the amount of $500 (the "Loan"). The Loan bears interest at a rate of 12% per annum and matures one year after the drawdown date of April 28, 2026, or such other date mutually agreed between the Company and Spirit (the "Maturity Date"). The Loan, together with accrued and unpaid interest thereon (the "Total Obligations"), are generally repayable at any time by the Company without penalty. If the Company has not repaid the Total Obligations before the closing of a sale of common shares in the capital of the Company, or units including common shares, in a single or series of transactions of no less than $1,000 (a "Qualified Financing") prior to the Maturity Date, the Total Obligations will be converted into the securities of the Company issued pursuant to the Qualified Financing ("Qualified Financing Securities") upon closing of the Qualified Financing (the "Conversion"), unless otherwise agreed between the Company and Spirit. The deemed price per Qualified Financing Security issuable upon Conversion will be the lowest price per Qualified Financing Security issued in the Qualified Financing, subject to customary adjustment provisions. The Conversion is conditional upon the completion of a Qualified Financing and receipt of the approval of the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Following the Annual General and Special Meeting of Shareholders of the Company held on May 14, 2026, Jean-Claude St Amour was appointed to the Company's board of directors. Along with the appointment, the Company also granted him 5,000,000 stock options pursuant to the 2024 Stock Option Plan. The stock options have an exercise price of $0.055 per share, with 1/3 of the options vesting immediately and 1/3 vesting on each of the first and second anniversaries of the date of grant. The stock options expire on the fifth anniversary of the date of grant.

Effective July 14, 2026, the Company entered into an unsecured loan agreement (the "July 2026 Loan Agreement") with Spirit for a non-interest bearing credit facility of up to $250 for working capital and general business purposes. Amounts advanced under the facility are due on July 14, 2027 (being one year from the first drawdown date), subject to a further one-year extension upon the mutual written agreement of the Company and Spirit. The Company drew $200 on July 14, 2026 and the remaining $50 on September 8, 2026, such that the facility is now fully drawn. The July 2026 Loan Agreement does not contain any conversion rights and amounts outstanding may be repaid by the Company at any time without penalty.

On August 31, 2026, the Company announced that Al Gourley resigned as a director of the Company effective August 31, 2026 and Brendan F.  Moore was appointed as Vice-Chairman of the board.

Effective September 11, 2026, the Company entered into an unsecured loan agreement (the "September 2026 Loan Agreement") with Spirit for a non-interest bearing credit facility of up to $250 for working capital and general business purposes. Amounts advanced under the facility are due on September 11, 2027 (being one year from the first drawdown date), subject to a further one-year extension upon the mutual written agreement of the Company and Spirit. The Company drew $250 on September 11, 2026, such that the facility is now fully drawn. The September 2026 Loan Agreement does not contain any conversion rights and amounts outstanding may be repaid by the Company at any time without penalty.

On September 14, 2026, the Company announced the appointment of Jean-Raymond Boulle II as Chief Executive Officer, effective October 1, 2026, replacing Lester Kemp.

Quarter End ResultsFor the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a net loss of $872 or $0.00 per share (2025 - net loss of $989 or $0.00 per share). The decrease in net loss was primarily due to the following:

  • Administration increased to $277 in 2026 (2025 - $196), mainly due to an increase in the fair value of share-based payments expensed. The fair value of share-based payments varies depending on the vesting of stock options granted.
  • Consulting and professional fees increased to $73 in 2026 (2025 - $47) due to higher legal fees incurred.
  • Corporate development decreased to $12 in 2026 (2025 - $102) due to reduced publication and communication costs.
  • Exploration and evaluation decreased to $474 in 2026 (2025 - $501) mainly due to lower depreciation of property, plant and equipment.
  • Unwinding of discount on environmental rehabilitation provision decreased to $20 in 2026 (2025 - $66). The decrease was primarily due to the reduction in the provision recorded 2025.
  • Change in derivative liability decreased to $nil in 2026 (2025 - $46) due to the changes in the fair values of the embedded derivatives of the convertible debentures.

Year to Date ResultsFor the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a net loss of $3,021 or $0.00 per share (2025 - net loss of $3,405 or $0.01 per share). The decrease in net loss was primarily due to the following:

  • Administration increased to $1,325 in 2026 (2025 - $1,000), mainly due to an increase in the fair value of share-based payments expensed. The fair value of share-based payments varies depending on the vesting of stock options granted.
  • Corporate development decreased to $53 in 2026 (2025 - $134) due to reduced advertising costs and publication and communication costs.
  • Exploration and evaluation decreased to $1,254 in 2026 (2025 - $1,431) mainly due to lower depreciation of property, plant and equipment.
  • Unwinding of discount on environmental rehabilitation provision decreased to $60 in 2026 (2025 - $198). The decrease was primarily due to the reduction in the provision recorded 2025.
  • Change in derivative liability decreased to $nil in 2026 (2025 - $264) due to the changes in the fair values of the embedded derivatives of the convertible debentures.

On September 30, 2026, the Company had $73 (December 31, 2025 - $724) in cash and cash equivalents and a working capital deficit (excess of current liabilities over current assets) of $1,097 (December 31, 2025 - working capital of $458). The decrease in working capital was a result of net cash used in operating activities.

A budget has been prepared for the completion of the PFS of $3,000. As of the date of this press release, the Company has undertaken work with SGS in respect of PFS engineering services, with expenditures estimated at approximately $137. The work completed to date includes the initial site visit by SGS's qualified persons and initial process design engineering services. The remaining work required to complete the PFS includes mining engineering, cost estimation, and civil engineering along with hydrogeological and geotechnical engineering. The Company currently estimates that the remaining work will require approximately $2,863 and will be completed within approximately 12 months after the necessary financing has been obtained, the required contractors have been scheduled and the work has recommenced.

The ability of the Company to continue as a going concern and fund its expenses in an orderly manner will require additional forms of financing. There can be no assurance that the Company will succeed in obtaining additional financing, now or in the future. Failure to raise additional financing on a timely basis could cause the Company to suspend its operations and planned activities.

data.title: Organigram Provides NASDAQ Listing Update
data.description:
Organigram Global Inc. () () (the “Company” or “Organigram”), Canada's #1 cannabis company by market share¹ and a growing global cannabis platform, today announced that on November 11, 2026, it received notification (the “Notification”) from The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) that it is not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) for continued listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The Notification was issued because the closing bid price of the Company's common shares was below US$1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days. Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) requires listed common shares to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share (the “Minimum Bid Requirement”), while Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a deficiency exists when the requirement is not met for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company's common shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has 180 calendar days, until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Company's common shares must be at least US$1.00 per share for a minimum of 10 consecutive business days during the compliance period, subject to Nasdaq's discretion to extend this period.

If the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, it may be eligible for an additional 180-calendar-day compliance period, subject to satisfying applicable Nasdaq requirements, including transferring its listing to the Nasdaq Capital Market. If the Company does not qualify for an additional compliance period, its common shares may become subject to delisting proceedings, subject to applicable appeal rights.

The Company's common shares are also listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, and the Notification does not affect the Company's listing or compliance status on that exchange.

About Organigram

Organigram Global Inc. is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market and TSX. The Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Organigram Inc., is a licensed cultivator and processor. Through its acquisition of Sanity Group GmbH ("Sanity Group"), Organigram participates in the German medical cannabis market and other emerging markets within Europe. Organigram is focused on producing high-quality cannabis for adult consumers, as well as extending the Company's global footprint. Organigram has also developed and acquired a portfolio of cannabis brands, including Edison, Big Bag O' Buds, SHRED, Monjour, Tremblant, Collective Project, Trailblazer, BOXHOT and DEBUNK. Through its acquisition of Sanity Group, Organigram's European brands include Vayamed, avaay, ZOIKS, Endosane Pharmaceuticals, VAAY, and Grashaus Projects. Organigram operates facilities in Moncton, New Brunswick and Lac Supérieur, Quebec, with a dedicated edibles manufacturing facility in Winnipeg, Manitoba. The Company also operates two additional cannabis processing facilities in Southwestern Ontario; one in Aylmer and the other in London. The facility in Aylmer houses best-in-class extraction capabilities, and is optimized for formulation refinement, post-processing of minor cannabinoids, and infused pre-roll production. The facility in London will be optimized for labelling, packaging, and national fulfillment. The Company is regulated by Health Canada under the Cannabis Act and the Cannabis Regulations.

data.title: More Than 10,000 Flights Delayed or Canceled in FAA's Nationwide Groundstop — WSJ
data.description:
By Andrew Tangel, Jacob Passy and Alison Sider

The Federal Aviation Administration halted departing flights nationwide Friday afternoon, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns after air-traffic control communications were disrupted.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote on X that there had been a communication issue affecting multiple air route traffic-control centers, which handle high-altitude flights covering large swaths of the country. "FAA technicians are investigating the issue," he wrote.

Planes in the air are able to continue flying to their destinations, an FAA spokeswoman said. Inbound international flights will be managed on a case-by-case basis, the agency said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House on Friday that "there was no prior indication, or indication as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us. This is a telecommunications outage as of now." When asked if it could be a cyberattack, Mullin said officials weren't ruling anything out yet.

"There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," Mullin said, adding this isn't "another 9/11."

The groundstop started Friday afternoon at 3:53 p.m. ET. More than 1,100 U.S. flights had been canceled and nearly 10,000 had been delayed as of Friday at 5:40 p.m. ET, according to FlightAware. As of around 4 p.m., there were still roughly 11,000 flights scheduled to depart from U.S. airports Friday, according to aviation analytics company Cirium.

On social media, travelers reported that taxiing planes were turned around at airports to return to gates and passengers were being deplaned, with flight crews signaling the delays could last hours. Others said they were stuck on aircraft as gates filled with passengers.

At Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, word quickly spread among travelers while ground traffic appeared to suddenly stop on the tarmac late Friday afternoon. By early evening, telecom issues at some FAA air-traffic facilities were coming back online, according to people familiar with the matter.

The outage appears to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to people briefed on the matter. The network handles crucial radio frequencies that air-traffic controllers use to communicate with pilots, the people said. It wasn't immediately clear whether the outage also affected the radar feeds that controllers use to keep aircraft safely separated in the skies.

An L3Harris spokeswoman didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

United Airlines said it is responding to the ground stop and will work with customers to get them to destinations once the issue is resolved. American said it expects its schedule to be disrupted for the rest of the day, depending how long the groundstop remains in place.

"It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop," American said in a statement.

More than 440 U.S. flights had been canceled and 9,000 had been delayed as of Friday at 5 p.m. ET, according to FlightAware.

John Sturino, a musician who plays the drums, said he is going to miss a percussion convention in Indianapolis because of the flight delay. The Brooklyn native said he had been waiting half an hour in line to cancel his flight at the Delta lounge desk in LaGuardia Airport and get a refund.

"It wasn't worth staying in the airport," he said.

Wedding photographer Christian Shackton was also waiting at LaGuardia Airport for a Southwest flight to Dallas for a work event. He considered himself lucky that he had already grabbed a spot at one of the terminal's restaurants before the flight delays began rolling in.

"The airport is a fun experience right now," he said. "If you're in a seat, stay in that seat or you will be fighting for a spot to relax while this gets sorted."

He said he had not yet received any notifications by email or through the Southwest app regarding the situation.

This is the second time in recent years the FAA has taken the extraordinary step of halting all departures across the country.

In 2023, a nationwide ground stop was ordered amid an outage of the FAA's Notice to Airmen system, which provides critical information to pilots. That order lasted for two hours, contributing to more than 1,000 flight cancellations. Before that, the FAA had only taken that step on Sept. 11, 2001.

The nation's air-traffic control system has been beset by communications issues leading to radio and radar outages that have affected various FAA facilities in recent years. Earlier this year, flights at New York-area airports were halted when a contractor accidentally cut a fiber communications line in New Jersey.

Other outages that have affected the Dallas area, Upper Midwest and New York City area have been relatively contained.

It wasn't immediately clear whether the telecommunications outages affected both radios controllers use to communicate with pilots, or also radar that they need to keep planes safely separated.

Updates to follow as news develops.

Write to Andrew Tangel at andrew.tangel@wsj.com, Jacob Passy at jacob.passy@wsj.com and Alison Sider at alison.sider@wsj.com

data.title: More gold analysts turning bearish as $4,000 support breaks
data.description:
As gold prices fail to hold above $4,000/oz, a growing number of analysts have noted that short-term momentum points to further price declines as rising bond yields and a stronger dollar continue to weigh on the metal.

Elevated inflation pressures and comments from Federal Reserve officials supporting a potential 50-bp rate hike next month are solidifying the market's hawkish bias, which leaves gold vulnerable to further selling pressure, Commerzbank commodity analyst Carsten Fritsch said in a note.

"Since Tuesday, the price has lost almost 7%, or around $290. Interest rate expectations have not risen that much since then, and bond yields are still below the level of early October," Fritsch wrote. "The risk is that ETF investors may start to sell in view of the price weakness. In this case, a further price decline would be expected."

Gold's recent selloff reflects more than a technical correction, as investors are being forced to reassess inflation risks and the Fed's monetary policy outlook, according to XS.com's Simon-Peter Massabni.

The dollar's rise to its highest level since April 2025 and elevated Treasury yields are creating significant obstacles for gold, Massabni said, and with the 10-year Treasury yield moving back above 5%, the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding precious metal continues to increase.

Gold's inability to hold support at $4K has created some technical chart damage, but investors should not confuse short-term weakness with the metal's long-term fundamentals, Saxo Bank's Head of Commodity Strategy Ole Hansen said in a note.

"Central banks continue accumulating bullion as part of their reserve diversification strategies, while ETF investors have demonstrated resilience despite recent volatility. These underlying sources of demand may help limit the correction but are unlikely to prevent further short-term weakness if yields and the dollar continue rising," Hansen wrote.

Gold futures finished little changed in choppy trading Friday, as a lower-than-expected U.S. producer price reading for October and steadier oil prices eased inflation concerns that weighed on prices in the previous session.

Front-month Comex gold for November delivery rose less than 0.1% to $3,879.70/oz, its second-lowest settlement value this year, and front-month Comex November silver slipped 1.9% to $49.031/oz, its lowest settlement value since November 7 last year.

For the full week, gold and silver fell 4.5% and 5.3%, respectively.

data.title: Fed Eyes Hedge Fund Leverage and AI Valuations as Risks — WSJ
data.description:
By Dylan Tokar

Highly leveraged hedge funds and pressures from elevated valuations of artificial intelligence companies are at the top of the Federal Reserve Board's list of potential risks to the financial sector.

The Fed identifies broad categories of risks in an annual financial stability report. Here are a few takeaways from the latest report, released Friday:

  • Hedge-fund leverage: Leverage of hedge funds reached the highest level since data became available in 2013, the Fed said. In contrast, the banking system is in a much better place than it was before the 2008 financial crisis, as banks have continued to modestly reduce their interest-rate risk.
  • Asset valuations: Asset valuations, in particular in equities, continued to be elevated, in large part due to market enthusiasm around AI. The central bank noted that some of the enthusiasm was moderated by concerns over capital expenditures and debt issuance plans. Along with equities, the Fed also noted climbing Treasury yields and increased volatility in the bond markets.
  • Private-credit redemptions: Funding risks remained moderate, the Fed said, noting that while redemption requests at some private-credit firms are elevated, they have been recently trending downward.

The Fed outlined several scenarios where one of the risks it had identified causes instability, including one where an unexpected downturn in corporate earnings sparks declines in corporate asset valuations-for example in the AI sector.

Another involved disruptive cyberattacks, including the potential for LLMs and agentic systems to exploit vulnerabilities in the financial system.

data.title: Trinity Place Holdings Inc. Reports Third Quarter Financial Results
data.description:
Trinity Place Holdings Inc. (OTC PINK: TPHS) (the "Company," "we," "our," or "us") today announced operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

The Company is an intellectual property holding, investment, and commercialization company. We own and control a portfolio of intellectual property assets focused on the consumer sector, a legacy of our predecessor, Syms Corp. (“Syms”), including FilenesBasement.com, as well as the intellectual property associated with the Running of the Brides® event and the An Educated Consumer is Our Best Customer® slogan. Our strategy today centers on monetizing these assets through brand licensing, e-commerce initiatives, strategic partnerships, and protection and enforcement of our intellectual property rights.

Net Operating Losses

At September 30, 2026, the Company had carryforwards of federal net operating losses (“NOLs”) of approximately $352.8 million available to reduce future federal taxes. Of the Company’s federal NOLs, $224.5 million were generated prior to 2018 and may expire if unused by 2037, and $128.2 million were generated in 2018 and later years and can be carried forward indefinitely subject to an 80 percent taxable income annual limitation.

Based on management’s assessment, it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets associated with the federal NOLs will not be realized by future taxable income or tax planning strategies. Accordingly, the Company has a valuation allowance of $74.1 million as of September 30, 2026. If our assumptions change and we determine that we will be able to realize these federal NOLs, the tax benefits relating to any reversal of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets would be recognized as a reduction of income tax expense and an increase in the deferred tax asset.

Note that our certificate of incorporation includes a provision intended to help preserve certain tax benefits primarily associated with our NOLs. This provision generally prohibits, subject to certain exceptions, transfers of stock that would result in a person or group of persons becoming a 4.75 percent stockholder, or that would result in an increase or decrease in stock ownership by a person or group of persons that is an existing 4.75 percent stockholder.
